discovery: High-precision Penning-trap mass spectrometry of short-lived exotic nuclei

nominees.name: Klaus Blaum
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute for Nuclear Physics, Heidelberg, Germany

nominees.name: Georg Bollen
nominees.affiliation: Facility for Rare Isotope Beams, Michigan State University, USA

nominees.name: Juha Äystö
nominees.affiliation: University of Jyväskylä and Helsinki Institute of Physics, Finland

motivation: The nominees made it possible to weigh radioactive nuclei that live only milliseconds with relative precisions of 1e-8 to 1e-9. Bollen and Blaum developed Penning-trap mass spectrometry for on-line radioactive beams at ISOLTRAP and later facilities. Their work includes buffer-gas cooling, cyclotron-resonance and phase-imaging detection, and coupling to fragmentation facilities. Äystö pioneered the IGISOL ion-guide technique, which gives fast, chemistry-independent access to refractory and fission-product nuclei, and with it the JYFLTRAP programme. Together these methods turned nuclear binding energies far from stability into precise, testable data. They revealed the evolution of shell closures and new magic numbers, tested CKM unitarity through superallowed beta decays, and supplied the masses that set r-process and rp-process paths in neutron-star mergers and X-ray bursts. These tools now underpin precision nuclear physics worldwide and connect the laboratory directly to the cosmic origin of the elements.
